title: Sequences and Why RNNs? ⏳
description: Discover sequential data and why standard neural networks struggle with order and memory.

slides.title: Life is Sequential 🔁
slides.content:
# Data with an Order

Many real‑world problems involve **sequences**:
- Text (words in a sentence)
- Speech (audio samples over time)
- Stock prices (daily values)
- Videos (frames in a clip)

In all these, **order matters**. Changing the order changes the meaning.

> Analogy: A sentence like "dog bites man" vs "man bites dog" – same words, different story.

slides.title: Feed‑Forward Networks Forget the Past 🧊
slides.content:
# Dense and CNN Limitations

- A standard Dense network treats each input independently. It has no memory of previous inputs.
- To process a sentence, you could feed all words at once (e.g., bag‑of‑words), but you lose word order.
- CNNs can capture local patterns (n‑grams) but still lack a true **memory state**.

Thus, we need a network that can **maintain a hidden state** that carries information across time steps.

quizData.question: Why can't a standard Dense network handle variable‑length sequences well?

options.text: It requires fixed‑size input and has no memory

quizData.explanation: Dense layers need a fixed input shape and process each sample independently without retaining past information.

slides.title: Recurrent Neural Networks – Memory Included 🧠
slides.content:
# The RNN Idea

A recurrent neural network has a **loop** that allows information to persist. At each time step, it receives an input **and** the previous hidden state, producing a new hidden state and an output.

> Analogy: Reading a book – as you read each word, your understanding (hidden state) is updated based on the new word plus your prior understanding.

slides.title: A Glimpse of an RNN Cell (Pseudocode)
slides.content: The heart of an RNN is a simple recurrence:
slides.codeSnippet:
# Pseudo‑code for a vanilla RNN cell
hidden_state = activation( input * W_xh + hidden_state_prev * W_hh + bias )

slides.title: Memory is the Key 🔑
slides.content: The hidden state is the network's **memory**. It learns what to keep and what to forget. RNNs are the foundation of modern NLP and time‑series models.
